intro: Meeting someone after a long time, asking how things are going, sending regards and saying a proper goodbye.
p.¿qué tal te va?: how are things going for you?
p.tirando.nota: From ir tirando: neither good nor bad.
p.¿cómo va lo de…?: how is that business of… going?
p.ir bien.nota: Me va bien: things are going well for me.
p.a ver si nos vemos: let's see if we can meet up
p.don.nota: Don José, doña Carmen: respectful, with the first name only.
b1.texto:
**Meeting again.** **¡Hombre, Luis!** **¡Cuánto tiempo!** **Me alegro de verte.** **¿Qué tal te va?** **¿Qué tal todo?**

The answers go beyond bien: **Estupendamente.** **Fenomenal.** **Todo bien, gracias.** **Tirando.** **Mucho mejor, por suerte.**

To ask about something specific, use **lo de**: **¿Cómo va lo de** tu piso? **¿Qué tal lo de** tu madre?

**Welcoming.** With the perfect subjunctive: **¡Qué bien que hayas venido!** **¡No sabes cuánto me alegro de que hayas venido!**

**Forms of address.** **Don** and **doña** go with the first name and show respect: **don Antonio**, **doña Pilar**. **Señor** and **señora** go with the surname: **el señor García**.

**Regards.** **Dale recuerdos a** tu madre **de mi parte.** **Dale un abrazo de mi parte.** **Ana te manda un beso.**

**Good wishes.** **Que te lo pases muy bien.** **Pásatelo bien.** **Aprovecha estos días.** **Te deseo lo mejor.** **Crucemos los dedos.** To someone ill: **Que te pongas bien pronto.** **Que se te pase.**

Returning them: **Lo mismo digo.** **Eso espero.**

**Goodbye.** **Hasta la próxima.** **A ver si nos vemos pronto.** **Espero que nos volvamos a ver.** **Ya sabes dónde tienes tu casa.**
b2.f0: Well, Teresa! Long time no see! I'm really glad to see you.
b2.f1: Paco! Likewise. How are things going for you?
b2.f2: Getting by. A lot of work, you know. And you? How's the shop business going?
b2.f3: Wonderfully. We open the second one next month. Fingers crossed.
b2.f4: I'm sure it will go very well for you. Hey, give my regards to don Ramón.
b2.f5: I will. Let's see if we can meet up soon, and have a great time on holiday.
b4.pregunta: Someone asks ¿Qué tal te va? and you are neither well nor badly. You say…
b4.o0.refuerzo: Tirando means getting by: neither well nor badly.
b4.o2.refuerzo: That returns a greeting or a wish.
b5.pregunta: Complete: how good that you have come!
b5.o0.refuerzo: A feeling about something already done: perfect subjunctive.
b5.o1.refuerzo: After qué bien que, the subjunctive.
b5.o2.refuerzo: After qué bien que, the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: Complete: give your sister a hug from me.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The phrase is de mi parte.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The phrase is de mi parte.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Don goes with the first name.
b7.o1.refuerzo: With a surname you use señor.
b8.o0: How is that business with your flat going?
b8.o0.explicacion: ¿Cómo va lo de tu piso? asks how the matter with your flat is going.
b8.o1: How do you get to your flat?
b8.o2: How is he going to your flat?
b8.o2.explicacion: Va here means is going, as in progressing.
b9.pregunta: Complete the wish: have a great time.
b9.o0.refuerzo: A wish with que takes the subjunctive, so pases is the right form.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Pasas is indicative; a wish with que needs the subjunctive, pases.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Pasarás is future; a wish with que needs the subjunctive, pases.
b10.traduccion: Let's see if we can meet up soon.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a dialogue between two old friends who meet by chance after ten years.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Play that meeting aloud: greet, catch up, send regards and say goodbye warmly.
